findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State service-user.sh's partial-failure/rollback behavior across its three sub-mutations (set-account, SSM overwrite, webhooks.config push), and add a recovery/re-run step if any sub-operation fails.
evidence: 'The canonical atomic tool is infra/gerrit/service-user.sh (gerrit set-account new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config to refs/meta/config).'

'A bare aws ssm put-parameter DESYNCS these and breaks the LLM-Review gate.' — the plan identifies desync as the core hazard but assumes service-user.sh is atomic across all three sub-operations without stating the rollback/recovery path on partial failure.
findings.finding: service-user.sh is called 'the canonical atomic tool' but performs three distinct mutations (gerrit set-account password, SSM overwrite, push webhooks.config to refs/meta/config) — the plan does not establish behavior on partial failure. If the Gerrit password is set but the SSM write or webhooks.config push fails, the shared secret DESYNCS mid-rotation, breaking the LLM-Review gate with the new password live in Gerrit but stale values in SSM/webhooks.config.
findings.location: 'Also: the token is a SHARED secret' and Step 2
scenarios: Gerrit set-account succeeds but the refs/meta/config push is rejected (stale ref / permission): inbound webhooks still send the OLD token while Gerrit basic-auth now expects the NEW one — split-brain until manually reconciled.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the deploy/restart steps with the unattended autodeploy loop (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh): re-VERIFY the running container to confirm whether 66af is already deployed (rather than asserting 'NOT deployed'), and either disable rebar-autodeploy.timer for the coordinated window (runbook: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`, re-enable after) or explicitly drive the deploy/restart through the loop, so the manual bounce cannot race an autodeploy tick.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:90 `BOT_PATHS='src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot ...'`; :276 `if changed "$BOT_PATHS" ...`; :359 `docker compose build "$BOT_SERVICE" && docker compose up -d` — the bot is rebuilt+recreated unattended (~2-min timer) on any src/rebar/ change

66af file_impact touches src/rebar/review_bot/app.py and src/rebar/review_bot/config.py, both inside BOT_PATHS — so the 66af image deploy is on autodeploy's AUTO-APPLY surface and was likely already shipped after the ~12:47 merge, contradicting the plan's 'image built BEFORE 1384 merged … 66af … NOT deployed' premise
Plan step 1: 'rebuild the compose-review-bot image from current main + docker compose up -d recreate' — the loop performs this unattended; plan never mentions autodeploy

autodeploy.sh:342-352 re-runs fetch-secrets.sh (SSM -> .env) BEFORE `compose up`, and :296-327 can DEFER or INTERRUPT an in-flight review on recreate — so a manual restart (step 3) can race an autodeploy tick or an autodeploy tick can recreate the container between rotate (step 2) and restart (step 3)

autodeploy.sh:96 notes a pure SSM VALUE rotation with no git change does NOT advance main, so the loop no-ops on it — confirming step 3's manual restart is genuinely required, which makes the race between manual restart and an unrelated autodeploy tick real
infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:443-448 documents `sudo systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer` as the back-out lever the plan could use to prevent the race during the coordinated window
findings.finding: The plan's manual deploy (step 1) and restart (step 3), and its 'NOT deployed to prod' decisive premise, do not model the unattended autodeploy loop that already auto-deploys the review-bot on src/rebar/ changes and re-runs fetch-secrets before `compose up` — creating a stale premise and a race during the coordinated bounce.
scenarios: Operator manually rebuilds (step 1) while an autodeploy tick is mid-recreate — doubling the bounce or interrupting an in-flight review
Operator reads 'NOT deployed' as still-true and treats step 1 as required, when autodeploy already shipped 66af — acting on a stale premise

An autodeploy recreation fires between step 2 (rotate) and step 3 (restart); it re-runs fetch-secrets and loads the new token fine, but a second interleaved tick or the manual restart fights the recreate and can interrupt a review with no operator visibility

Rewrite step 1 to note the loop may have already deployed 66af (so step 1 is verify-not-necessarily-rebuild), and step 3 to note the timer is disabled so the manual `compose up -d` cannot race an autodeploy recreation that would re-run fetch-secrets.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the deploy/restart steps with infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh: re-verify the running container (rather than assume 'not deployed', since 66af touches BOT_PATHS and may already be auto-shipped), and state how the manual deploy/rotate/restart avoids racing the ~2-min loop (e.g. pause/hold the autodeploy timer or flock for the rotation window, and note that a pure SSM value rotation does not advance main so autodeploy will not re-fetch the new token unaided).

66af file_impact touches src/rebar/review_bot/app.py and config.py — both inside BOT_PATHS — so 66af's image deploy is on autodeploy's auto-apply surface; since 66af is MERGED to main, the loop may already have shipped it, making the plan's 'NOT deployed to the prod box' premise potentially stale

autodeploy.sh:349 re-runs fetch-secrets.sh (SSM -> .env) BEFORE `compose up` on a bot/secrets redeploy — a recreation between plan steps 2 (rotate) and 3 (restart) would itself reload the token, and could fight the operator's manual `docker compose up -d`

autodeploy.sh:296-317 drain-defer gate can recreate the container mid-review once the DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX bound is exhausted, so a manual bounce during the coordinated window can collide with an autodeploy tick
Plan quote (step 1): 'rebuild the compose-review-bot image from current main + docker compose up -d recreate' — a manual action the loop performs unattended; the plan never mentions autodeploy at all
findings.finding: The plan's manual deploy (step 1) and restart (step 3) do not reconcile with the unattended autodeploy.sh loop that already auto-deploys the review-bot on the exact paths 66af touches and re-runs fetch-secrets.sh on every bot/secrets redeploy — an out-of-band actor that can make the 'not deployed' premise stale, race the manual bounce, or load a stale/rotated token between rotate and restart.
scenarios: Operator acts on the 'not deployed' premise and manually rebuilds while autodeploy has already shipped 66af (step 1 is a silent no-op / double bounce)
An autodeploy tick recreates the container between rotate (step 2) and manual restart (step 3), or races the manual `compose up -d`
A recreation during the coordinated bounce interrupts an in-flight LLM-Review the plan intended to protect by choosing a quiet window
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step 0 that (a) checks the actual container image/config to confirm whether autodeploy already deployed 66af, and (b) quiesces the autodeploy loop (stop/mask its systemd timer or hold its deploy flock) for the duration of steps 1-3, restoring it after step 4's verification — so the coordinated deploy-rotate-restart cannot race an unattended tick.

scenarios: service-user.sh sets the new Gerrit password and SSM but the outbound basic-auth vote fails in step 4, leaving the LLM-Review gate broken with no documented recovery
webhooks.config push conflicts on refs/meta/config, leaving inbound secret desynced from SSM
